scope: Simulator-only Compose configuration; not host packages or other deployments

rules.name: removed-perl-runtime
rules.reason: Perl interpreter executables are removed. The application contains no Perl embedding or invocation. Scanner source-package metadata is retained; this is component removal, not a claim that Perl 5.40.1 is patched.

rules.name: removed-mount-and-namespace-tools
rules.reason: Affected command-line entrypoints are removed. Compose runs non-root, with all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges and no setuid/setgid executables in runtime paths. The privileged mount/cgroup operations required by these advisories are unavailable in this deployment.

rules.name: removed-gnu-gzip
rules.reason: The GNU gzip executable is removed. The affected multi-file LZW/LZH decoder is not Python's gzip/zlib library or Node's zlib, which the application uses.

rules.name: removed-infocmp
rules.reason: The advisory affects analyze_string in the infocmp command-line program, which is removed. Other ncurses binary packages share the scanner source-package association, not that entrypoint.

rules.name: no-systemd-homed
rules.reason: systemd-homed is absent and no homed-managed user/home service exists. The affected component is not libsystemd/libudev, although they share a Debian source package.

rules.name: no-privileged-acl-caller
rules.reason: The advisory requires a privileged pathname-based ACL caller operating on attacker-replaceable paths. Runtime UIDs are non-root, permitted/effective/bounding capabilities are zero, no-new-privileges is active, and setuid/setgid executables are absent. Application routes do not invoke ACL operations. This conclusion does not cover root/admin maintenance shells or a changed deployment.

rules.name: sqlite-fts5-reachability
rules.reason: The vulnerable system SQLite library is present but its FTS5 malicious-database/MATCH path is not reachable in this simulator deployment. Python constructs PostgreSQL and AsyncQdrantRemote, verified inside each Python image with SQLite connections forbidden. All 40 real-service integration tests pass with SQLite forbidden in durability test processes. Node and Qdrant binaries do not link system SQLite; the Qdrant SBOM has no compiled Rust SQLite dependency. Application source has no SQLite imports, SQL/database-upload endpoint, native-plugin loading or arbitrary scripting. This is a deployment-specific reachability assessment, not a patched-library claim; adding any SQLite path requires a new review.
